keys.label: Anti-aliasing method
keys.desc: Smooths jagged edges. MSAA looks cleanest but costs the most FPS; FXAA is cheap but makes the picture a little soft.

keys.label: MSAA samples
keys.desc: How many samples are used to smooth each edge. 4x is the usual sweet spot; 8x suits screenshots or a strong graphics card.

keys.label: MSAA edge blending
keys.desc: How the smoothed edge samples are blended together: soft, neutral, sharp or the old method.

keys.label: Shadow maps
keys.desc: Turns on real-time shadows from the sun. One of the biggest FPS costs in the sim.

keys.label: Shadow detail
keys.desc: How many shadows are drawn. 0 draws fewer, 1 draws as many as possible.

keys.label: Car shadows (day)
keys.desc: Shadows cast by cars and other moving things in daytime. Costs CPU for every car on screen.

keys.label: Trim small shadow casters
keys.desc: On skips small objects when drawing car shadows, which saves work. Off keeps more of the shadows.

keys.label: Car shadow resolution
keys.desc: How sharp car shadows look. Only matters while car shadows are on.

keys.label: Track shadow maps
keys.desc: How many high-quality shadow layers are used for the track and its surroundings (3 to 8).

keys.label: Track shadow resolution
keys.desc: How sharp the track shadows look. Mostly uses graphics card memory and power.

keys.label: Object self-shadowing
keys.desc: Lets trackside objects cast shadows on themselves. iRacing support says this can hurt performance.

keys.label: Night shadow maps
keys.desc: Real-time shadows at night, cast by the track and car lights.

keys.label: Night shadow filter
keys.desc: How soft night shadow edges are. iRacing warns the higher steps can cause stutter; PCF4 is the safe step.

keys.label: Night shadow lights
keys.desc: How many lights cast shadows at night. iRacing advises 3 or fewer.

keys.label: Night wall shadows
keys.desc: Track walls cast shadows at night.

keys.label: Night object shadows
keys.desc: Trackside objects, like signs and buildings, cast shadows at night.

keys.label: Night shadow sampling
keys.desc: 0 works out night shadows more exactly; 1 is a bit faster but slightly softer.

keys.label: Night shadow fade-in
keys.desc: How long night shadows take to fade in, in hundredths of a second. Has no effect on FPS.

keys.label: Shadow lights per pass
keys.desc: How many shadow-casting lights are handled at once (0 to 6). The default is fine.

keys.label: Ambient occlusion
keys.desc: Adds soft darkening in corners and where objects meet. A subtle effect that costs graphics card power.

keys.label: Reflections (SSR)
keys.desc: Reflections of the scene on wet track and shiny paint. Costly, and mostly noticeable in rain.

keys.label: Reflections only in rain
keys.desc: With reflections on, 1 shows them only in wet sessions.

keys.label: Fixed cubemaps
keys.desc: How often reflections of the surroundings are refreshed on fixed objects (100 = every frame). Costs CPU and graphics card.

keys.label: Dynamic cubemaps
keys.desc: How often reflections of the surroundings are refreshed on moving cars (100 = every frame). Costs CPU and graphics card.

keys.label: Headlight quality
keys.desc: How good the headlight beams look at night.

keys.label: White headlights
keys.desc: All-white headlights avoid blotchy bands of light; colored headlights look more realistic.

keys.label: Sky update rate
keys.desc: How often the sky and clouds are redrawn.

keys.label: Particle detail
keys.desc: How good smoke, dust and sparks look.

keys.label: Full-resolution particles
keys.desc: Draws smoke and spray at full sharpness instead of half. Costs only graphics card power.

keys.label: Lens distortion
keys.desc: A lens-warping effect on replay cameras. Purely a look choice.

keys.label: Heat haze
keys.desc: The heat shimmer behind hot cars. Purely a look choice.

keys.label: Depth of field
keys.desc: Blurs things in the background or foreground. Purely a look choice.

keys.label: Motion blur (broadcast cams)
keys.desc: Motion blur on TV and replay cameras only.

keys.label: Motion blur (driving cams)
keys.desc: Motion blur while driving. It makes the picture less clear, so most racers leave it off.

keys.label: Motion blur strength
keys.desc: How strong the blur is: off, low, medium, high or ultra.

keys.label: Cars drawn
keys.desc: The most cars drawn in the main view (10 to 64). Every extra car costs CPU, which is usually the limit for FPS.

keys.label: Cars drawn in mirrors
keys.desc: The most cars drawn in each mirror (4 to 64). Too low and cars behind you can disappear.

keys.label: Pit objects in mirrors
keys.desc: How much pit equipment is drawn in each mirror (0 to 192).

keys.label: Cockpit mirrors
keys.desc: How many real mirrors in the car (0 to 4). Each one is a big FPS cost; the on-screen virtual mirror is cheaper.

keys.label: Mirror detail
keys.desc: How detailed things look in the mirrors: 0 is low, 1 is high.

keys.label: Car detail
keys.desc: How detailed the car models look.

keys.label: Mirror detail floor
keys.desc: The most detail mirrors can show. Below 100 adds detail and costs FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Mirror detail ceiling
keys.desc: How far mirror detail may drop to save FPS. Above 100 trades detail for FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Mirror detail floor (adaptive)
keys.desc: Same as the mirror detail floor, but for the setting that adjusts itself to your FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Mirror detail ceiling (adaptive)
keys.desc: Same as the mirror detail ceiling, but for the setting that adjusts to FPS. Already at its top in the Race preset. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Hide cockpit obstructions
keys.desc: Hides the halo, A-pillar and roll cage so they don't block your view. Down to your preference.

keys.label: Driver hands
keys.desc: Shows the driver's hands on the wheel. Down to your preference.

keys.label: Steering wheel
keys.desc: Shows the steering wheel: none, yes, fixed, or only if it has a display. Down to your preference.

keys.label: Virtual mirror
keys.desc: The rear-view mirror shown on screen. Cheaper than real mirrors in the car, so it is kept on.

keys.label: Headlights in mirrors
keys.desc: Headlights light up the track in the mirrors. Kept at the Race preset value.

keys.label: Reduce cockpit flicker
keys.desc: Reduces shimmering on parts of the cockpit. A compatibility setting, left as is.

keys.label: 2048 car paint textures
keys.desc: 0 uses 1024-pixel car textures, 1 uses sharper 2048-pixel ones. 2048 takes much more video memory.

keys.label: Swap high-res nearest cars
keys.desc: Puts higher-resolution textures on the nearest cars. Memory handling, left as is.

keys.label: Object detail
keys.desc: How many objects are placed around the track.

keys.label: Grandstand detail
keys.desc: How detailed the grandstands look.

keys.label: Crowd
keys.desc: The spectators in the stands. You barely notice them while driving, but they show in replays.

keys.label: Pit object detail
keys.desc: How detailed the pit equipment looks.

keys.label: Foliage
keys.desc: How many trees and bushes there are. A clear visual change on wooded tracks.

keys.label: Event detail
keys.desc: Extra detail around the race weekend scene.

keys.label: Pit objects drawn
keys.desc: The most pit objects drawn per camera (0 to 192).

keys.label: Two-pass trees
keys.desc: Draws trees in two steps for cleaner edges. Costs graphics card power.

keys.label: Low-quality trees
keys.desc: 1 draws simpler trees, 0 draws full-quality trees.

keys.label: Swaying trees
keys.desc: Trees move in the wind. Purely cosmetic.

keys.label: Track surface relief
keys.desc: Gives the track surface real bumps and curbs. Costs graphics card power only.

keys.label: Tire marks
keys.desc: Rubber marks left on the track.

keys.label: Shader quality
keys.desc: How good materials, car paint and lighting look.

keys.label: HDR rendering
keys.desc: Brighter highlights and deeper darks in lighting. A look choice that also changes how bright the scene is.

keys.label: Auto exposure
keys.desc: Adjusts brightness to the scene, like your eyes adapting. Only works when HDR is on.

keys.label: Sharpening
keys.desc: Adds a sharpening effect. A matter of taste; it can look artificial.

keys.label: Sharpening strength
keys.desc: How strong the sharpening is, 10 to 300 (default 125).

keys.label: Sharpening limit
keys.desc: Caps how harsh the sharpening can get, 0 to 100 (default 10).

keys.label: Texture sharpness bias
keys.desc: Shifts how sharp textures look, in percent. Positive is blurrier, negative is sharper.

keys.label: Resolution scaling
keys.desc: Draws below your screen resolution and scales it up. Saves graphics card power only; it won't help if your CPU is the limit.

keys.label: Upscaler sharpness
keys.desc: How much the scaled-up picture is sharpened. Only used with resolution scaling on.

keys.label: Contrast
keys.desc: How strong the light-dark difference is, -6 to +6. Down to your preference.

keys.label: Brightness
keys.desc: How bright the scene is, -6 to +6. Down to your preference.

keys.label: Gamma
keys.desc: Shifts the brightness of midtones, -6 to +6. Down to your preference.

keys.label: 32-bit depth buffer
keys.desc: More precise depth handling so surfaces don't flicker. A system setting, left as is.

keys.label: Detail floor
keys.desc: The most detail cars and objects can show. Below 100 adds detail and costs FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Detail ceiling
keys.desc: How far detail may drop when your FPS sags. Above 100 trades detail for FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Detail floor (adaptive)
keys.desc: Same as the detail floor, but for the setting that adjusts itself to your FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Detail ceiling (adaptive)
keys.desc: Same as the detail ceiling, but for the setting that adjusts to FPS. Lower is better quality.

keys.label: Detail drop FPS target
keys.desc: Detail is lowered whenever FPS falls below this number. Lower means fewer detail drops. iRacing doesn't document the limits.

keys.label: Stop objects vanishing
keys.desc: Stops detail from dropping so far that an object disappears from view completely.

keys.label: Occlusion culling
keys.desc: Skips drawing things hidden behind other things. iRacing says leave it on.

keys.label: Multithreaded scene sort
keys.desc: Uses several CPU cores to prepare the scene. Leave it on.

keys.label: Visibility re-test delay
keys.desc: How many frames pass between checks for what is visible. A fine-tuning detail, left as is.

keys.label: Near clip distance
keys.desc: How close an object can be before it stops being drawn, in tenths of a metre (1 to 30). Fine-tuning, left as is.

keys.label: Load textures while driving
keys.desc: 0 loads textures only when you are out of the car. Left as is.

keys.label: Compress car textures
keys.desc: Shrinks car textures to save video memory. iRacing highly recommends it.

keys.label: Compress helmet textures
keys.desc: Shrinks helmet textures to save video memory.

keys.label: Compress suit textures
keys.desc: Shrinks driver suit textures to save video memory.

keys.label: Compressed vertices
keys.desc: Stores 3D model data in a smaller form. Left as is.

keys.label: NVIDIA Reflex
keys.desc: NVIDIA's low-latency mode: off, on, or on+boost. Reduces input lag; doesn't change the picture.

keys.label: Max pre-rendered frames
keys.desc: How many frames the graphics card may lag behind the CPU (0 to 4). 1 is normal.

keys.label: V-Sync
keys.desc: Locks frames to your screen's refresh rate. Off can show tearing but avoids added input lag.

keys.label: Multi-GPU count
keys.desc: How many graphics cards are linked together (SLI or CrossFire). Always 1 here.

keys.label: VR mode
keys.desc: The way the sim draws for VR headsets. Not used on a monitor, so RaceMode never writes it.

keys.label: System memory for iRacing
keys.desc: How much of your PC's memory iRacing may use, in MB. Depends on your PC, so RaceMode never writes it.

keys.label: Video memory for iRacing
keys.desc: How much graphics card memory iRacing may use, in MB. Depends on your card, so RaceMode never writes it.

keys.label: UI size
keys.desc: Size of the on-screen interface, in percent. Set it in the sim.

keys.label: Replay render modes
keys.desc: Stylized replay looks such as black and white or VHS. Leave off for normal use.

keys.label: Limit frame rate
keys.desc: Turns the FPS cap on or off. RaceMode never writes it here; only the screen check can keep it, and only if you turn that on.

keys.label: FPS limit
keys.desc: The FPS cap. RaceMode never writes it here; only the screen check can keep it, and only if you turn that on.
